original_question: Let H be the partially ordered collection of irreducible subset systems on Top0, let HR be the induced irreducible subset system of H-Rudin sets, and define R : H -> H by R(H) = HR. If H has property M, must R be a closure operator, that is, monotone, expansive, and idempotent?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1: for an R-subset system H having property M, is the assignment R(H)=H^R a closure operator on the poset 𝓗 of all R-subset systems? The paper then resolves this positively via Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3. ([pmf.ni.ac.rs](https://www.pmf.ni.ac.rs/filomat-content/2024/38-30/38-30-25-24604.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft has the right target: it asks about the operator sending an R-subset system H to the induced system H^R of H-Rudin sets, and it correctly identifies the three closure-operator axioms that the paper asks about—monotonicity, expansiveness, and idempotence. It also correctly keeps the hypothesis involving property M, which is part of the paper’s official question before the paper proves that property M is automatic. ([pmf.ni.ac.rs](https://www.pmf.ni.ac.rs/filomat-content/2024/38-30/38-30-25-24604.pdf))
missing_details: The ambient ordered class should be the family 𝓗 of all R-subset systems H: Top_0 -> Set, ordered by H_1 <= H_2 iff H_1(X) ⊆ H_2(X) for every T_0 space X, rather than a single symbol H being used both for the ambient poset and for one element of it. ([pmf.ni.ac.rs](https://www.pmf.ni.ac.rs/filomat-content/2024/38-30/38-30-25-24604.pdf))

The paper-faithful notation is H^R (the induced R-subset system of H-Rudin sets), not a subscripted H_R. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0166864120304922?utm_source=openai))

To be stand-alone, the question must define an H-Rudin set: A subset A of a T_0 space X is H-Rudin when cl_X(A) is a minimal closed member of M(K) for some K in H(P_S(X)). ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0166864120304922))

The question should define M(K) and m(K): M(K) = {C in Γ(X) : C ∩ K != empty for all K in K}, and m(K) is the set of minimal members of M(K). ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0166864120304922))

The hypothesis 'H has property M' needs its exact content: for every T_0 space X, every K in H(P_S(X)), and every A in M(K), the family {upward(K ∩ A) : K in K} belongs to H(P_S(X)). ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0166864120304922))

The question should specify that P_S(X) is the Smyth power space of X, since H(P_S(X)) appears in both property M and the definition of H^R. ([pmf.ni.ac.rs](https://www.pmf.ni.ac.rs/filomat-content/2024/38-30/38-30-25-24604.pdf))

It helps to state explicitly that the reason property M appears in the original formulation is to ensure that H^R is again an R-subset system, so that R is a self-map on 𝓗. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0166864120304922))
refined_question: Let 𝓗 be the poset of all irreducible subset systems (R-subset systems) H: Top_0 -> Set, ordered by H_1 <= H_2 iff H_1(X) ⊆ H_2(X) for every T_0 space X. For such an H and a T_0 space X, define H^R(X) to be the family of H-Rudin sets of X, where A ⊆ X is H-Rudin if cl_X(A) belongs to m(K) for some K in H(P_S(X)); here P_S(X) is the Smyth power space, M(K) = {C in Γ(X) : C ∩ K != empty for all K in K}, and m(K) is the set of minimal members of M(K). Assume H has property M, namely that for every T_0 space X, every K in H(P_S(X)), and every A in M(K), the family {upward(K ∩ A) : K in K} lies in H(P_S(X)). Must the operator R: 𝓗 -> 𝓗, defined by R(H)=H^R, be a closure operator; that is, must it be monotone, expansive, and idempotent? ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0166864120304922?utm_source=openai))
equivalent_formulation: Because Proposition 1.2 proves that every R-subset system has property M, the paper treats the above as equivalent to asking whether, for every R-subset system H, the assignment R(H)=H^R defines a closure operator on 𝓗. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.11299))
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at the paper’s closure-operator question, not at the neighboring problems about products, equalizers, or reflections of super H-sober spaces. The official formulation reproduced in the surrounding literature is: 'Let H : Top_0 -> Set be an R-subset system having property M. Is R : 𝓗 -> 𝓗, H ↦ H^R, a closure operator?' The arXiv abstract of 2109.11299 confirms that this paper proves that every R-subset system naturally has property M and derives the corresponding consequences, which matches the paper’s introduction-level packaging as Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, and Theorem 1.3. What your draft still lacked for stand-alone precision were the ambient poset 𝓗, the exact order relation, the paper’s notation H^R, and the definitions of H-Rudin sets and property M. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.11299))
